provenance: Official source: yes. This data is BetaNYC's, derived from it, not an official Metropolitan Transportation Authority record.
Read-only requests to MTA's public feed when a tool is called, with no API key. Each response is kept in memory for up to 60 seconds, so an answer can lag the feed by about a minute.

Changed by BetaNYC: BetaNYC does not alter MTA's values. Each answer uses part of the feed: the alerts for the route, date or station asked about, and the English text where MTA gives one. MTA's terms allow an app to use some but not all of the data. Next to MTA's fields, BetaNYC adds its own reading: an effect from MTA's alert type, whether it counts as a disruption, and in check_route_on_date a yes-or-no answer. These are BetaNYC's, not MTA's data. In the answers, BetaNYC's reading of each alert is kept in a separate betanyc object. Stop names are added from the station list (topic stations); check_route_on_date can add the station's accessibility status and elevator outages; get_service_alerts counts the alerts that BetaNYC reads as disruptions.

dataset.scopeNote: Known gap: Only what MTA puts in the feed at the moment of the request. Past alerts that MTA has removed from the feed cannot be looked up. Caveat: MTA publishes no refresh cadence for this feed, and answers can be up to a minute old, so every answer is marked as possibly not real time. Caveat: Which stops an alert affects comes from the alert's own list of stops, not from MTA's wider list of stations on the route.

provenance: Official source: yes. This data is BetaNYC's, derived from it, not an official Metropolitan Transportation Authority record.
Read-only requests to MTA's public feeds when a tool is called, with no API key. Each response is kept in memory for up to 60 seconds.

Changed by BetaNYC: BetaNYC does not alter MTA's values. Each answer uses part of the feed: the outages for the station, line or date asked about. MTA's terms allow an app to use some but not all of the data. In a separate betanyc object on each row, BetaNYC adds the station the outage is placed at, found by joining MTA's equipment number to MTA's elevator inventory (topic elevator-inventory) or, when that fails, by matching MTA's station name; how it was matched; a note when the evidence is mixed; and the inventory's details for that equipment, including MTA's alternate route. These are BetaNYC's additions, not MTA's data.
